correctness.rationale: An exact five-symbol local bijection characterizes every labeled inclusion-maximal matching of C_n square K_2 for each integer n>=3; matching degrees and uncovered adjacent vertices are tested with necessary-and-sufficient local conditions. The fully specified 25-state weighted transfer matrix has an exact degree-eight determinant reconstructed with integer-polynomial Newton identities, yielding the all-order trace-log formula. The formal change t=s/y^2,z=y^3 provides a nonnegative y-degree certificate k>=ceil(2n/3) and derives the three exact positive minimum-layer coefficients. Independent exhaustive recursion enumerates all candidate matchings for n=3..12 and compares entire polynomials; these finite tests are corroborative, not the general proof. Definitions, labeling, excluded short cycles, and normalization are explicit.

originality.rationale: Full graded maximal-matching polynomial for the cyclic prism with sharp minimum-layer multiplicities is not logically implied by the previously published ungraded prism sequence A284703 or maximal-matching enumeration of open ladders. The exact known prism total is expressly credited: D(t,1) equals the OEIS scalar denominator. Multiple exact-claim, synonym, and reduction searches, plus material comparison with full primary text, found no encompassing prior theorem. Residual risk of a bivariate prism formula under another label remains and search non-detection is not proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: Older or non-English literature may tabulate prism maximal-matching polynomials under saturated dimers, maximal independent edge sets, or edge domination polynomials.

value.rationale: The complete graded distribution of saturated dimers on a two-row periodic strip is a natural all-order cardinality invariant, determining occupancies and finite-size statistics that the known scalar OEIS total does not. The sharp minimum and the exact three-residue counts of its attainment describe meaningful worst-case saturation and are proved by a structural generating-function argument; the result is neither a small finite census nor an arbitrary parameter restriction.
